ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the circle $\odot O$, the diameter $CD$ is perpendicular to the chord $AB$ at point $E$, and $OB$ and $BC$ are connected. Given that the radius of $\odot O$ is $2$ and $AB=2$, what is the measure of $\angle BCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that diameter $CD$ is perpendicular to chord $AB$ at point $E$, and $AB=2$,\\
it follows that $\angle OEB=90^\circ$, and $BE=1$,\\
since $OB=2$,\\
thus $\angle BOE=30^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BCD=\boxed{15^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is circle O; the vertical line CD passes through the center O of the circle and is a diameter; the horizontal chord AB intersects CD at point E, and there is a right-angle mark at E, indicating CD ⟂ AB. Point B is at the lower right of the circle; OB and BC are connected in the figure, and the angle sought is ∠BCD, whose vertex is at C and whose two sides are CB and CD. Reasoning: Because diameter CD passes through the center O of the circle, and CD is perpendicular to chord AB at E, the perpendicular from the center of the circle to the chord bisects chord AB, so E is the midpoint of AB. Given AB=2, so BE=1. Also OB is a radius of the circle, and the radius is 2, so OB=2. In right triangle OEB, ∠OEB=90°, and sin(∠BOE)=BE/OB=1/2, so ∠BOE=30°. Since E, O, and D are on the same diameter CD, OD and OE are in the same direction, so ∠BOD=30°. ∠BCD is an inscribed angle, intercepting the same arc BD, and its corresponding central angle is ∠BOD, so ∠BCD=1/2×30°=15°.
